stories.title: Chinese national Li Ming charged in fraud case in Singapore linked to Megaspeed and Alice Huang: Report
stories.summary: Li Ming, a Chinese national, is facing fraud charges in Singapore regarding alleged transshipment of Nvidia chips. He was involved with Megaspeed, a company linked to Alice Huang, the former romantic partner of Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang. Li is accused of misleading an American supplier by misrepresenting the intended destination of purchased servers. Following an investigation, Megaspeed was placed on a no sell list by Nvidia.
stories.headline: Chinese National Charged in Singapore Nvidia Chip Fraud Case

unclustered.title: Claude Code Has Been Leaking Secrets Through Its "Don't Ask Again" Feature
unclustered.summary: Agentic security firm Apiiro found that Claude Code has been exposing secrets in public repositories due to how it stores them in local file on developers' machines to implement "Don't Ask Again". The company identified 1,122 secrets in claude/settings.local.json files and another 1,160 in git history, in the shared settings.json, and in agent chat transcripts stored in repos. By Sergio De Simone
unclustered.headline: Claude Code Leaks Secrets Through 'Don't Ask Again' Feature

unclustered.title: Google Announces Agent Compute Engine for Secure AI Agent Execution
unclustered.summary: Google recently announced Agent Compute Engine, a managed service that runs AI agents in isolated microVMs, with checkpointing capabilities to suspend and resume execution environments. The design keeps credentials, API keys, and OAuth refresh tokens outside the agent sandbox, using an external Agent Gateway to authenticate requests and inject the required secrets. By Renato Losio
unclustered.headline: Google Launches Agent Compute Engine for Isolated AI Agent Execution

unclustered.title: AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
unclustered.summary: Scientists have developed an AI tool that can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85% of cases in a major study involving nearly 70,000 patients. By revealing subtle patterns that conventional screening misses, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and spare patients unnecessary invasive procedures.
unclustered.headline: AI Detects Bladder Cancer Five Years Before Diagnosis

unclustered.summary: AWS Lambda now runs Event Functions on EC2 G-series GPU instances through Lambda Managed Instances, with up to 48 concurrent invocations sharing one model per GPU, vLLM and SGLang base images that need no handler code, and 90-minute asynchronous timeouts. unclustered.title: Hillclimbing AISafetyResearchBench
unclustered.summary: AI labs' main alignment strategy is using AIs to uplift AI safety research. This way, as AIs get smarter (and likely harder to align?), we also enhance our safety-research capabilities and our understanding of "Misalignment Science".One way to use AI to speed up AI safety research is to delegate "number-go-up tasks” to AIs. Number-go-up tasks are problems with a numeric, easily verifiable output, so anyone can measure how well a task was done. This makes them suitable to delegate to AIs (even potentially untrusted AIs). Some examples: auditing games, “ARC-like” white-box challenges, jailbreaks robustness, various small model post training challenges or RL from sparse reward[1], etc. Fully automating number-go-up tasks isn't sufficient to fully automate AI-safety research. Human researchers still have to decide which metrics are worth maximizing and why. Some problems are also harder to turn into number-go-up tasks at all, such as some flavors of adversarial robustness, or whether a saf
unclustered.headline: AI Labs Test Hillclimbing for Safety Research Uplift
